'''Clive Robert Humby''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE}} (born 3 February 1955) is a British [[mathematician]] and [[Entrepreneurship|entrepreneur]] in the field of [[data science]] and customer-centric business strategies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.managementtoday.co.uk/mt-britains-top-100-entrepreneurs-2007/article/625114|title=MT Britain's Top 100 Entrepreneurs 2007|website=www.managementtoday.co.uk|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> Since 2014, he has been Chief Data Scientist of the consumer insights company, Starcount.<ref name=join>{{Cite web|url=http://www.harnham.com/post/2013-8/edwina-dunn-and-clive-humby-to-join-starcount|title=Edwina Dunn and Clive Humby to Join Starcount|website=Harnham|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Humby was born in [[Leicester]]. He attended [[University of Sheffield|Sheffield University]] from 1972 to 1975, graduating with a B.Sc. in Applied Mathematics & Computer Science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/alumni/news/hon-grads-summer-2016-1.594467|title=Clive Humby|website=The University of Sheffield - Alumni|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

== Career ==
Humby joined American data analysis specialists [[CACI]] in 1976.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/companies/article/we-know-what-you-put-in-your-shopping-basket-blbl5x97m85|title=We know what you put in your shopping basket|date=2011-01-16|work=The Sunday Times|access-date=2019-04-30|issn=0956-1382}}</ref>

He worked on a project that used data from the 1970 census to plan locations for [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] recruitment offices following the abolition of the draft.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.statslife.org.uk/features/2816-understanding-the-customer-through-their-data-an-interview-with-clive-humby|title=Understanding the customer through their data: an interview with Clive Humby {{!}} StatsLife|website=www.statslife.org.uk|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> He returned to CACI’s UK office in 1977 and contributed to the development of the [[Acorn (demographics)|Acorn]] classification system.{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}}

In 1989, Humby left CACI to become joint founder and Chief Data Officer of global consumer insights business, [[dunnhumby]], with his wife and long-term business partner, Edwina Dunn.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-30095454|title=The couple who changed the way we shop|last=Smale|first=Will|date=2014-11-24|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> The company applied science and technology to customer data, to help businesses understand consumer trends and behaviours.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/women/womens-life/11394755/Married-to-the-job-what-its-like-to-work-with-your-partner.html|title=Married to the job: what it's like to work with your partner|last=Shuckburgh|first=Hannah|journal=Daily Telegraph|date=2015-02-14|access-date=2019-04-30|issn=0307-1235}}</ref> From their relationship with [[Tesco]], they launched the [[Tesco Clubcard|Clubcard]] in 1995 - the first mass customisation loyalty programme in the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://moneyweek.com/419435/profile-of-edwina-dunn-and-clive-humby/|title=How Edwina Dunn and Clive Humby launched the Clubcard|date=2015-12-21|website=MoneyWeek|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> Dunnhumby has offices in 25 countries employing 1500 people.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.owler.com/company/dunnhumby|title=Dunnhumby Competitors, Revenue and Employees - Owler Company Profile|website=Owler|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

In 2006, Humby coined the phrase “Data is the new oil”.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/aug/23/tech-giants-data|title=Tech giants may be huge, but nothing matches big data|last1=Arthur|first1=Charles|date=2013-08-23|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-04-30|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Michael Palmer expanded on Humby's quote by saying, like oil, data is “valuable, but if unrefined it cannot really be used.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ana.blogs.com/maestros/2006/11/data_is_the_new.html|title=Data is the New Oil|last1=Palmer|first1=Michael|website=ANA Marketing Maestros|access-date=2021-05-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tdwi.org/articles/2019/04/22/data-all-how-data-is-like-oil.aspx|title=How Data Is (And Isn't) Like Oil|last1=Firican|first1=George|date=April 22, 2019|website=Transforming Data with Intelligence|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> [Oil] has to be changed into gas, plastic, chemicals, etc to create a valuable entity that drives profitable activity; so, data must be broken down and analysed for it to have value.”<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://medium.com/project-2030/data-is-the-new-oil-a-ludicrous-proposition-1d91bba4f294|title="Data is the New Oil" — A Ludicrous Proposition|last=Haupt|first=Michael|date=2016-05-02|website=Medium|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

Humby and Dunn sold their stake in dunnhumby to Tesco in 2011. In 2012, they set up H&D Ventures, a business and data science team exploring the possibilities of telecoms and financial services data.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thedrum.com/news/2013/08/07/social-media-analytics-firm-starcount-acquires-tesco-clubcard-creators-hd-ventures|title=Social media analytics firm Starcount acquires Tesco Clubcard creators' H&D Ventures business|website=The Drum|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> In 2013, they became investors in Purple Seven, a theatre and arts analytics company, to evaluate the cultural behaviour of 19 million UK consumers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Graham |first=Natalie |date=2013-08-30 |title=Edwina Dunn: Clubcard founder's points to success |url=https://www.ft.com/content/b25ea6a8-0fe2-11e3-99e0-00144feabdc0 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2019-04-30 |website=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref>

In 2014, Humby was invited to join Starcount as Chief Data Scientist and the company acquired H&D Ventures in the process.<ref name=join/> Starcount is a data and analytics consultancy focused on exploring and extracting data-based insights.

Humby espouses "The Power of Two" leadership principle. This teaches that the most effective way to operate is by pairing two people with complementary skills, e.g., analysts and marketers. It is a model he and Dunn instigated at dunnhumby, and which he continues to advocate to this day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thesupperclub.com/insights/axa-growth-leaders-series-the-power-of-two|title=AXA Growth Leaders Series - The Power of Two Edwina Dunn|website=www.thesupperclub.com|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He married [[Edwina Dunn]] in 1982. They have two children.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.managementtoday.co.uk/sleeping-business-partner/article/1286952|title=Sleeping with your business partner|website=www.managementtoday.co.uk|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref>

Humby is a trustee of the [[Royal Academy of Arts|Royal Academy]], as well as chairman of the Friends of the Royal Academy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Royal Academy Development Trust {{!}} Royal Academy of Arts |url=http://www.royalacademy.org.uk/royal-academy-trust |access-date=2019-04-30 |website=www.royalacademy.org.uk}}</ref>

== Board directorships and honours ==
He was awarded an [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] for "services to Data and UK Business" in the [[2019 Birthday Honours]].

He is on the retail advisory board of [[LetterOne]], an international investment business.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.letterone.com/our-businesses/l1-retail/our-team/clive-humby/|title=Clive Humby - LetterOne|website=www.letterone.com|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> He is also a board director of [[Holland & Barrett]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-40400216|title=Holland & Barrett sold for £1.8bn|date=2017-06-26|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

Humby holds honorary doctorates in engineering from the University of Sheffield, and in Business Administration from [[Kingston University|Kingston University London]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/alumni/news/hon-grads-summer-2016-1.594467|title=Honorary Graduates recognised during summer graduation 2016 - News - Alumni - The University of Sheffield|last=Sheffield|first=University of|website=www.sheffield.ac.uk|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> He is an Honorary Companion of the [[Operational Research Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theorsociety.com/what-we-do/awards/companion-of-or/previous-awards/|title=Previous Awards - The OR Society|website=www.theorsociety.com|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref> He holds Honorary Fellowships of the Institute of Mathematics and its Applications, the Institute of Direct & Digital Marketing, and the [[Market Research Society]] of which he is also Patron.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.performingartistes.co.uk/artistes/clive-humby|title=Clive Humby - Leading marketing analyst and specialist in customer retention|website=www.performingartistes.co.uk|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mrs.org.uk/about/fellows|title=Fellows & Patrons {{!}} Market Research Society|website=Market Research Society|access-date=2019-04-30}}</ref>

== Books ==
Humby is a coauthor with Terry Hunt and Tim Phillips of the book ''Scoring Points: How Tesco is Winning Customer Loyalty'', on the history of the Tesco Clubcard.<ref>Reviews of ''Scoring Points'':
*Geoff Plimmer (2010), ''Journal of Revenue and Pricing Management'', {{doi|10.1057/rpm.2010.17}}
*Merlin Stone (2003), ''Journal of Database Marketing & Customer Strategy Management'', {{doi|10.1057/palgrave.dbm.3240219}}</ref>
